turns.text: A plant. Everyone's bringing plants. I will have a jungle and no idea how to keep it alive.

turns.speaker: Joaquin
turns.text: I'll bring a cactus. Impossible to kill.

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: I killed a cactus in 2022.

turns.speaker: Joaquin
turns.text: How?

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: Watered it every day. I thought I was being nice.

turns.speaker: Joaquin
turns.text: Plastic plant it is.

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: Perfect. The deposit on this place was $2,100 so I can't afford real plants anyway.

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: Did you move the router? The wifi in my room has been dead since like Saturday.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: I moved it behind the bookshelf because the blinking light was keeping me up.

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: Kellan. The bookshelf is basically a wall of encyclopedias. Nothing is getting through that.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: Okay, fair. I'll put it back on the hallway table tonight.

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: Thank you. I have my thesis draft due to Dr. Obuya on the 16th and I can't keep working from the Lantern Street library.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: Wait, I thought your draft was due at the end of May?

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: It was. She gave me an extension because of the lab flood. So June 16th now.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: Lucky. Oh, also, the landlord texted. Rent is going up to 1,420 in August.

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: From 1,350? Ugh. So we're each paying 710.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: Yeah. Unless you want to finally take the bigger room and pay more, like you kept saying you would.

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: I said MAYBE. And that was before the rent went up.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: Ha, noted. Router tonight, I promise. Maybe I'll just tape over the light.

turns.speaker: Moira
turns.text: Genius. Truly an engineer.

turns.speaker: Kellan
turns.text: I'll take that as a compliment.

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: Are you going to the all-hands on Friday or are you 'working from home' again?

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Ha. I'll be there. I have to present the Q3 numbers for the Halbrook account, remember?

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: Oh right. How's that looking?

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Revenue's up about 8 percent, but we lost two of their smaller shops. Pennard told me not to lead with that.

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: Pennard also told us the new coffee machine would be here in July.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Ha, yeah. I heard from Lise in facilities that it's actually coming October 3rd. We'll see.

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: I'll believe it when I taste it. Are you doing anything after the all-hands? A few of us are going to Tidewell Tavern.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: I can't, I've got a physio appointment at 5:15. My knee's been bad since the charity run.

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: The 10K? I thought you said you barely ran it.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: I walked half of it. My knee doesn't care about the details.

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: Fair. Next time. Oh, and don't forget your badge, they're doing the security check again.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Right, badge. Knee brace. Slides. Got it.

turns.speaker: Rhiannon
turns.text: And maybe don't mention you walked half the 10K in front of the fundraising people.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: My lips are sealed.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: What are you doing for New Year's?

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: Honestly? Nothing. I'm going to sleep at ten and feel great about it.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Liar. Last year you said that and ended up at Marguerite's until 3am.

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: That was different, she had a karaoke machine. I'm only human.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Well Ines is hosting this year. Board games, potluck, starts at eight.

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: What board games? If it's that farming one again I'm out.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Probably. She just bought the expansion. But also Codewords, I think.

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: Okay I'm maybe in. What do I bring?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: She said drinks or dessert. I'm bringing my lemon bars.

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: The good lemon bars or the ones you made in October?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Those were fine!

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: They were soup, Nadia. Delicious soup. I'll bring a cheese plate.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Rude. See you at eight. Ines's place is on Wickmoor Road now, she moved in November.

turns.speaker: Ferris
turns.text: Wickmoor, got it. I'll try not to fall asleep by ten.

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: Did you finish the dungeon last night?

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: Almost. I got to the final boss and the game crashed. Lost like an hour.

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: No autosave?

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: It autosaves, but only when you rest at a lantern, and I was being greedy.

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: Classic. I beat it on Saturday. Took me eleven tries.

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: Eleven? You told Magnus it took you three.

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: I told Magnus it took me three because Magnus did it in two and I have pride.

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: Your secret's safe. Kind of. Are you coming to game night Thursday?

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: Thursday at Magnus's? I thought it moved to Friday.

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: It did, then his sister needed the living room Friday, so it's back to Thursday. Seven-thirty.

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: Okay, Thursday seven-thirty. I'll bring the new card game I got at Rookery Games.

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: The one with the ducks?

turns.speaker: Corentin
turns.text: The one with the ducks. It's twenty-two dollars of chaos.

turns.speaker: Bex
turns.text: Perfect. I'll try not to crash.

turns.speaker: Lucian
turns.text: Did you end up buying the couch?

turns.text: The green one from Fernhollow? No. I went back and sat on it again and it felt like sitting on a sandwich.

turns.speaker: Lucian
turns.text: A sandwich.

turns.speaker: Marisol
turns.text: Like, too soft in the middle and crunchy at the edges. I don't know how else to describe it.

turns.speaker: Lucian
turns.text: Okay. So what now?

turns.speaker: Marisol
turns.text: I ordered a grey one online instead, 899 plus delivery. It comes on the 12th.

turns.text: Online? Without sitting on it?

turns.speaker: Marisol
turns.text: It has 2,000 reviews, Lucian. And you can return it in 30 days.

turns.speaker: Lucian
turns.text: Return a couch. Through your third-floor stairwell. Sure.

turns.speaker: Marisol
turns.text: Okay, when you say it like that. But I'm confident.

turns.speaker: Lucian
turns.text: You said you were confident about the bike too.

turns.speaker: Marisol
turns.text: The bike was a great purchase! I just don't ride it.

turns.speaker: Lucian
turns.text: That's... not how great purchases work.

turns.speaker: Marisol
turns.text: Help me carry the old couch down on the 12th and I'll buy you dinner.

turns.text: How's the ankle?

turns.text: Better. The doctor said it's a sprain, not a break, thank god.

turns.speaker: Ignatius
turns.text: What happened, again? You were very vague in the group chat.

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: I tripped over a rake. In my own garden. That I had left there myself.

turns.speaker: Ignatius
turns.text: Oh no. That's worse than I imagined.

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: I know. I told Rosalind it was a 'hiking injury.' Please don't correct her.

turns.speaker: Ignatius
turns.text: Your secret is safe. How long till you're back to running?

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: Four to six weeks, she said. So probably I miss the Kindlewood half-marathon on December 7th.

turns.speaker: Ignatius
turns.text: Ugh, you trained for that since summer.

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: Since August. But there's another one in March, in Delford. I might do that one instead.

turns.speaker: Ignatius
turns.text: Might?

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: Might. If I don't trip over anything else first.

turns.speaker: Ignatius
turns.text: I'll come over and hide your rake.

turns.speaker: Pernille
turns.text: Please. Hide all the rakes.

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: Honestly? Behind. The client changed the colour scheme again yesterday.

turns.speaker: Anneliese
turns.text: Again? That's the third time.

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: Fourth. They went from blue to green to blue and now 'warm teal.'

turns.speaker: Anneliese
turns.text: What even is warm teal.

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: Nobody knows. Maxine's making three versions so they can pick.

turns.speaker: Anneliese
turns.text: And the launch was supposed to be February 10th.

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: It's going to be the 24th now. I told their project manager on the phone this morning and she said fine, surprisingly.

turns.speaker: Anneliese
turns.text: Did she put that in writing?

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: Not yet. I'll email her today so we have it.

turns.speaker: Anneliese
turns.text: Good. Last time Brockley swore they'd agreed to a delay and then billed us for it.

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: Right, never again. Email first, coffee second.

turns.speaker: Anneliese
turns.text: Coffee first, you'll write a better email.

turns.speaker: Rafferty
turns.text: Coffee first. Email second. Warm teal forever.

turns.speaker: Rafferty

turns.speaker: Rafferty

turns.speaker: Rafferty

turns.text: Why do I always get the pans?

turns.speaker: Imogen
turns.text: Because you're the one who burned the rice into the big pot on Sunday.

turns.speaker: Nadia

turns.speaker: Holm
turns.text: Wait, it did? You never said. Okay, definitely dumplings.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: You did. On the phone. You said "sure whatever."

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Sounds like me. How much was it?

turns.speaker: Priya

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Then we're not late. Is Benedek still helping?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: He says yes but he also said yes to the last move and showed up at two with a coffee.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Right. So we plan without him. What about the couch, is it even going to fit through the new door on Ardley Lane?

turns.speaker: Dev

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The landlord said we can't leave anything on the landing, fire rules. So you're not.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Fine. Then we take the legs off. Remind me to find the Allen key, I think it's in box fourteen.

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: Game night is still on for Friday, right?

turns.speaker: Rosalind
turns.text: Friday the 5th, my place, seven-ish. Bring snacks that aren't just crisps.

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: Wow, rude. What are we playing?

turns.text: Ilka said Cartographers of Brine took an hour and we were there until one in the morning.

turns.text: That was a gesture of passion. How many people?

turns.speaker: Rosalind

turns.text: Please do. Those are the only reason people like you.

turns.speaker: Kenji
turns.text: Honestly, fair.

turns.speaker: Rosalind
turns.text: Oh, and actually make it half six, not seven. My neighbours complain after eleven.

turns.speaker: Pascal

turns.speaker: Gunnhild
turns.text: Of course you did. I'll take a photo of mine and send it. There's a table with all the flats.

turns.speaker: Pascal
turns.text: Thank you. Do they say who's paying?

turns.speaker: Gunnhild
